subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should OpenClaw treat configured model refs that are absent from the trusted runtime/provider catalog as warnings, hard validation errors, or keep the current suppression-only behavior?
rationale: The code path is clear, but changing catalog absence from accepted config into a diagnostic or error affects forward-compatible model names, custom providers, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Advisory catalog warnings
options.body: Warn in `config validate` and doctor for absent catalog refs while allowing forward-compatible/custom configs to keep running.

options.title: Fail validation for unknown refs
options.body: Reject absent catalog refs during config validation, maximizing early detection but risking breakage for custom or newly released models.

options.title: Keep suppression-only checks
options.body: Continue rejecting only known retired/suppressed models and rely on runtime fallback notices for other catalog misses.

recommendation.title: Advisory catalog warnings
recommendation.body: Warn in `config validate` and doctor for absent catalog refs while allowing forward-compatible/custom configs to keep running.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on `src/config/validation.ts`, where amknight has the strongest recent history signal among the identified owners.
